# Answer-key scorecard

*Generated by `analysis/build_plan.py` from `analysis/scorecard/frozen_estimates.json` and, once received,
`analysis/scorecard/answer_key.json`. Rules: [analysis/scorecard.py](../analysis/scorecard.py) ·
deviations: [DEVIATIONS.md](../analysis/scorecard/DEVIATIONS.md).*

**Status: no answer key is available — 43 parameters frozen, none scored.**

Every estimate and 90% interval below was frozen before any answer key was seen (first as `estimates-frozen-v1` in commit [`52f856e`](https://github.com/Akshith597/bramblewood-analytics-engineering/commit/52f856ef95bea644fe6d9a72227a966af36c8f65), then
re-frozen as `estimates-frozen-v2` in commit [`515cb99`](https://github.com/Akshith597/bramblewood-analytics-engineering/commit/515cb99366cc295692149941945a64aad9831de9) when the methods were simplified, and re-frozen as `estimates-frozen-v3` when a promotion-date fix moved the elasticities slightly; see the deviation log). Scoring uses that file, not a re-run, and a test fails if any current result differs from it. A truth
inside the interval counts as covered; with honest intervals about 90% should be.

The dataset was generated by AI ([provenance](../data/SOURCE_README.md)). The brief mentions a generator and answer key, but neither is in this repository and no public copy could be found, so it is unknown whether a key exists. If one is obtained, truth, error and coverage fill in automatically when it is committed as `analysis/scorecard/answer_key.json`. Until then, the estimates are checked only by the planted-effect, backtest and second-implementation checks in the [decision memo](decision_memo.md#how-the-results-were-checked).

## What the scorecard proved wrong

Nothing: no answer key is available, so no estimate has been tested against ground truth. This section lists every parameter whose 90% interval misses the truth, with the claims it touches.

## What the physical records proved wrong before the key

- **The $1.05M forecast figure** was planned units, not stock: stores received 0.9% more than they sold, and comparable-store stock rose $19.4K on average.
- **"Apply the bias correction now"**: on an inventory replay the correction finds no saving at each forecast's best safety stock (−$941.32).
- **Bias on clean weeks would be lower**: it is higher (+19.3%), because stock-out weeks are the weeks the forecast under-calls.
- **The README** still said promotions and out-of-stock cost were "not yet answered" after the memo had answered them; it is now rendered from results and checked in CI.
